To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated c.w. parametrization in GeAsSe PCFs, which have the highest nonlinearities and lowest losses among all fiber platforms in the MIR.
we have demonstrated the first mid-infrared (MIR) continuous-wave (c. w.) parametric amplification and conversion in a chalcogenide photonic crystal fiber.
we demonstrate c.w. paramteric amplification in chalecogenide microstructure fibers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel waveguide structures and devices for the efficient use and manipulation of nonlinear optical effects in the mid-infrared (MIR) region.
the development of new materials and structures for nonlinear optics in the MIR, and in particular for the development of new sources and components for the MIR.
the development of a novel class of optical fibers that are capable of generating and manipulating light in the mid- and long-wavelength infrared (MIR and LWIR) spectral regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown the first c.w., mid-infrared parametric amplification using tapered PCFs, which opens the way to a new generation of compact and efficient sources for the mid-infrared.
the authors have demonstrated a new platform for MIR c.w.-parametric amplification in GeAsSe PCFs, with the potential for high efficiency and broad bandwidth, paving the way for new MIR applications.

the authors have experimentally demonstrated the first c.w parametric amplification at 2 micron in a fiber waveguide, and have established GeAsSe PCFs as the most promising high efficiency MIR parametric converter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the first c.w., parametric amplifier in the MIR using an all-fibered platform.
the GeAsSe PCFs are the best waveguides for MIR nonlinear processes.
we have demonstrated the first c.w., parametric amplifier in the mid-IR using a chalcogenide PCF taper.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a PCF geometry in a tapered fiber configuration allows us to achieve a combination of low propagation losses, high nonlinearity (up to 2000 W−1  km−1 at 2 µm) and low dispersion (down to 10 ps  km−−1 at 3 μm) in a single fiber.
the combination of high nonlinearities and low dispersion can now be achieved with low-loss single-mode fibers.

, in addition to the already demonstrated high nonlinearity in Ge10As22 Se68 PCF, the fiber tapering technique enables a further improvement in the conversion efficiency, which is essential for the development of compact and efficient fiber parametric sources in the MIR.
